newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish banking sector net profit doubles in H1 '96.
newsitem.headline: Polish banking sector net profit doubles in H1 '96.

text.p: Polish banks netted 2.9 billion zlotys in the first half of 1996, compared with 1.3 billion in the same period of last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said Wednesday.
GUS said bank revenues had increased by 26.2 percent to 16.7 billion zlotys in the period, while costs rose by 14.1 percent to 12.8 billion zlotys.
It said private banks had registered the fastest growth of the profit-to-revenue ratio, with the pre-tax profit ratio growing to 36 percent and the net profit to 24 percent.
The profit-to-revenue ratio was lower for state-owned banks, with pre-tax ratio rising to 23 percent and net profit ratio to 16.7 percent.
Co-operative banks' profit-to-revenue ratio grew slowest, at 14.3 and 10.9 percent for pre-tax and net respectively.

For the banking sector as a whole the pre-tax profit to revenue ratio increased to 23.6 percent from 15.5 in the first half of 1995, while the net profit ratio to 17.2 percent from last year's 9.5 percent.
About 90 of Poland's banks took part in the GUS survey.
